text.intro:
Which measurement carries the Addis offset: an answer to the question the 9 Nov status page left open, from data already in
hand (233 Addis filters of the 7 Nov closeout, and the IMPROVE record of thermal EC and HIPS). **The aethalometer is not used**: the
Addis MA350 is not a reference. A results page, not a recorded meeting. Exploratory: no Addis filter has thermal (TOR) EC, so the absolute
level stays a range. Written account: docs/addis-reference-closure-2026-11-10.md.
text.improve:
**IMPROVE's own thermal EC shows HIPS falling behind as the filter darkens.** 347,936 IMPROVE samples
(210 sites, 2005-2025) have TOR EC and HIPS on the same day. Grouped by the previous sample's EC loading at the site,
so that neither instrument's error decides the group, HIPS Fabs ÷ TOR EC falls from 13.1 m²/g on the
lightest filters to 8.4 at optical depth 0.94. A saturating curve through the group
medians has a **ceiling of 2.26** (1.82–2.70, resampling sites); the low-OC/EC sites and
the six urban IMPROVE sites give the same. Addis optical depth has a median of 0.96 and reaches 1.51, so
Addis sits on the bend. No FTIR and no aethalometer enter this. **The ceiling is not the same in every period:** 2.53
for 2005–2014 and 1.71 (1.34–2.36) for 2015–2025, the years
that include the Addis record. The later value predicts an Addis exponent of 0.42, which is what Addis
shows, and a positive intercept (+2.25). So the ceiling is the main uncertainty: it decides whether the
intercept left after linearising is slightly negative, zero or positive, though not whether the −6 goes away.
text.addis:
**At Addis, HIPS and FTIR EC are far from proportional, and the IMPROVE curve predicts most of it.** HIPS rises as FTIR EC
to the power 0.46 (instrument: gravimetric PM2.5) or 0.41
(XRF potassium); with no instrument at all the exponent is bounded to 0.39–0.54. If FTIR EC were exactly proportional
to EC, the IMPROVE curve predicts 0.56 (0.46–0.64)
at Addis optical depths. So HIPS compression accounts for most of the departure from 1. What is left over is small and not resolved:
a ceiling at the low end of its interval, or FTIR EC rising a little faster than EC. 233 Addis filters; 188 with
PM2.5 mass, 189 with a published EC.
text.response:
**Linearising HIPS with the IMPROVE ceiling takes the intercept to zero.** The published fit moves from
2.31x − 6.17 to **0.55x +0.01**
(intercept +1.59 to -0.97 across the ceiling's interval). The correction is large
(median × 1.74) and multiplies noise on the heaviest filters. Against linearised HIPS, FTIR EC is close to
proportional but not exactly: linearised HIPS rises as FTIR EC to the power 0.85
(0.78–0.92). The slope that remains is the level question: FTIR EC would
need a MAC near 19 m²/g to agree.
text.season:
**Most of the seasonal swing was HIPS; a smaller one remains, and lot 248 reads low.** Against HIPS as measured, FTIR EC ÷ HIPS
goes from 0.84 in Bega to 1.29 in Kiremt within lot 251. Against
linearised HIPS it goes from 0.51 to 0.60. Kiremt
also has the heaviest filters, so season and loading cannot be told apart here. Lot 248 reads lower than lot 251 in the same season
against linearised HIPS (0.40 vs 0.51 in Bega) and
against PM2.5 mass (0.16 vs 0.20), so that offset is not a HIPS effect.
text.level:
**The slope that is left has two parts, and they fit together.** After linearising, FTIR EC is 0.55 of
HIPS BC at MAC 10. That is the FTIR level times 10 ÷ the real MAC. On the urban IMPROVE sites the raw-spectra calibration reads
0.91 of thermal EC, and the published product reads 1.11× that calibration at Addis. If the same bias
holds at Addis, the slope implies a MAC of about 19 m²/g; IMPROVE's urban sites give 16.4 on light filters and the five
Adama filters about 19. **Working range: published EC × 1.0 to 1.4, most likely about × 1.1.** The anchors put published ÷ true between
0.70 and 1.15. Mass closure caps it: published EC reconstructs 89 % of gravimetric PM2.5, × 1.5 reaches
100 % and × 1.9 gives 108 %. None of this is thermal EC measured at Addis, and section 8 shows why IMPROVE
cannot settle it.
text.network:
**Across SPARTAN, the exponent falls with a site's optical depth about as the IMPROVE curve says, but one ceiling does not suit
every site.** Addis is the heaviest site (median optical depth 0.95) and the least proportional
(0.46 measured, 0.57 predicted). Linearising takes the Addis intercept from
-6.22 to -0.18 µg/m³, Delhi from -1.77 to
-0.41, Santiago from -1.33 to -0.35 and Beijing from
-0.55 to -0.05. It moves the intercept toward zero at 6 of the 12
sites with a readable exponent. It over-corrects where HIPS and FTIR EC were already close to proportional at moderate optical depth:
Pretoria (-0.07 to +0.45), Johannesburg, Jaipur, Mexico City and Dhaka
(-1.93 to +2.44). The two Chilean sites are far less proportional than their optical
depth predicts with either instrument (0.56), which is a real difference, not noise. Pick a site below to see its filters.
text.candidates:
**Every saved calibration loses its intercept and more than half of its seasonal swing once HIPS is linearised.** Across the twelve
calibrations the Addis intercept runs from -10.3 to -1.0 µg/m³ against HIPS as measured and from
-1.0 to +0.6 against linearised HIPS. For the published product, Kiremt reads
1.63× Bega as measured and 1.28× once linearised. What remains differs by calibration: the spline
baseline keeps 1.18×, the full-spectrum calibrations about 1.3×. That is consistent with a composition-linked part in
FTIR (more organic signal in Kiremt), but season and loading still cannot be separated at Addis.
text.source:
**FTIR does read thermal EC low on Addis-like IMPROVE filters, by about a tenth, not a quarter.** The closeout's heavy low-OC/EC
subset (TOR EC ≥ 15 µg, TOR OC/EC < 2.5) gives FTIR ÷ TOR of 0.78. But that subset is chosen by each filter's own TOR
values, so it collects filters whose TOR EC happened to read high, and the ratio comes out too low. Choosing by the previous sample at the
site gives 0.91 (0.87–0.94); the six urban IMPROVE sites give 0.91 (0.88–0.94).
The saved calibrations then differ little: 0.82 to 0.92 on the urban sites, against
0.65 to 0.85 on the selected subset. FTIR EC is proportional to thermal EC there
(exponent 0.94, 0.90–0.98), and lot 248 reads no lower than lot 251.

**IMPROVE cannot say what the bias is at Addis.** With EC and OC calibrations fitted the same way on both, Addis FTIR OC/EC has a median of
0.98; 99 % of Addis filters are below IMPROVE's 5th percentile (1.94), and the
urban IMPROVE median is 3.65. The bias grows as OC/EC falls across IMPROVE sites
(0.96 at site OC/EC 3.5–5, 0.93 at 2.5–3.5),
so it is probably larger at Addis, by an amount no IMPROVE filter can show. IMPROVE is a mostly rural and remote network; "urban" here means
its six city sites (Atlanta, Birmingham, Fresno, Phoenix, Pittsburgh, Seattle), which are its low-OC/EC end.

**A correction cannot be learned by binning on OC/EC.** In the lowest bin the same IMPROVE filters read
0.62 of thermal EC when binned by TOR's own OC/EC and 1.54 when binned by
FTIR's own. Each ratio contains the error of the EC it is built from, so the bin collects that error.

**The Adama TOR filters help with the MAC, not with the FTIR level at Addis.** The five Adama pairs are the only thermal EC in Ethiopia.
They carry 7 µg of EC per filter at TOR OC/EC 6.1; Addis filters carry about 34 µg at an OC/EC near 1. So Adama sits at
the opposite end from Addis, where the calibrations disagree most (FTIR ÷ TOR from 0.96 to 2.23 across four
calibrations on three clean pairs). What Adama does show: per unit of thermal EC, HIPS reads 15 to
17 m²/g there, above IMPROVE's curve at the same optical depth. Ethiopian aerosol absorbs more per unit EC than
MAC 10 assumes, which is the other half of the 0.55 slope.
text.mac:
**The MAC you believe decides the FTIR level.** Once HIPS is linearised, the published FTIR EC agrees with HIPS only if the MAC is
18.7 m²/g (between 16.1 and 24.2 across the ceiling's interval). At the conventional MAC of 10, FTIR would be
reading 0.53 of true EC. But every MAC measured against thermal EC is above 10: 13.1 m²/g on light IMPROVE
filters, 16.4 at IMPROVE's six urban sites, and 15.9 on the five Adama filters (18.9 after the same
linearisation). At the urban IMPROVE value FTIR reads 0.88 of true EC; at the Adama value, 1.01.
Adama is the only thermal EC in Ethiopia, so it is the most relevant MAC and the least certain: five filters, another site and sampler.
text.steps:
**Both next steps are now run.** *EPO, re-scored.* No saved EPO predictions exist, so EPO was refitted on the raw spectra with the
repository's own implementation, inside each training fold. On IMPROVE's six urban sites it reads 0.93
(0.88–0.98) of thermal EC against 0.91 for
the plain calibration: a small real gain, at the cost of a higher median error overall (1.42 against
1.27 µg per filter).

*What the calibration responds to.* Across IMPROVE site means, the raw calibration's prediction is 0.9 µg per filter plus
**0.78 × thermal EC** (0.69–0.84) plus 0.015 × OC. It under-responds to EC and makes up the
difference with a fixed offset, which works at IMPROVE's loadings and not at Addis's. Blank filters show an offset too, a larger one: the calibration reads
2.2 µg of EC on IMPROVE field blanks and 2.7 µg on
Addis field blanks. EPO raises the gain to 0.89 and removes the OC response. Read at Addis loading and an OC/EC of 1, the raw
calibration gives 0.82 (0.75–0.87) of true EC and EPO 0.91
(0.81–1.00). That is a linear extrapolation, not a measurement.

*Spectral augmentation.* Co-adding three urban IMPROVE filters on one blank gives 53 µg of EC, an Addis-like loading, and FTIR reads
0.83 of it. But for a linear calibration that number is exactly the sum of the three predictions minus twice the blank reading, so
co-adding shows the offset and nothing else, and a sum can never have a lower OC/EC than its parts. Augmentation cannot test Addis composition.
text.next:
**Proposed position.** Carry the published FTIR EC forward with no intercept correction and a stated level range. Stop using
Fabs / 10 as the Addis yardstick without linearising. A modest season or loading effect and a lot-248 offset remain open. The proposed TOR
pass band (0.8 to 1.25) now contains the most likely answer (about 0.9 to 1.0), with the lower edge still inside the plausible range
(0.7 to 1.15). Ten pairs fix a mean bias only to about ±27 % (3 Nov simulation), which is wider than the question that is left, so decide before they
arrive whether the deliverable is pass or fail, or an estimated level factor, and ask for HIPS on the same filters with a few loaded to Addis optical depth. Optical agreement is still not thermal EC.
